title: Crustal dichotomy in the South China coastal region revealed by seismic data
abstract: Continents with thinned crust constitute a significant portion of the global landmass, but the detailed crustal structure varies across regions, and the causes of this variation remain debated. The Cathaysia block in South China—a typical region characterized by a thinned crust—provides a natural laboratory to investigate the underlying mechanisms. In this study, we deployed dense seismic arrays in the central part of the Cathaysia block to image the detailed crustal structure using receiver function analysis. We observe a consistently thin crust (~30 km) and a relatively flat Moho in the entire region, confirming previous results with new seismological constraints. Moreover, the receiver functions display a dichotomic crustal structure across the region bounded by the Zhenghe-Haifeng fault and the Chao’an-Puning fault, with weak intra-crustal conversions in the northwest compared to the complex layering southeastward. We validate this dichotomy with Moho reflections extracted from ambient noise data and find correspondingly large amplitude differences. Combined with regional gravity and geochemical data, our observations suggest that slab rollback and delamination might have jointly shaped the crust of the Cathaysia block during the Late Mesozoic, punctuated by localized crust-mantle interaction. Similar processes may occur in other regions characterized by thinned crust.
